prompts.label: WHAT IS VPC CIDR AND SUBNETS?
prompts.placeholder: A VPC is an isolated virtual network with one or more IP address ranges. A…

reveal.text: A VPC is an isolated virtual network with one or more IP address ranges. A subnet is a non-overlapping range inside the VPC and belongs to one Availability Zone.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Plan CIDRs with enough usable addresses and no overlap with networks that must connect.

reveal.text: Plan CIDRs with enough usable addresses and no overlap with networks that must connect.

A VPC uses `10.0.0.0/16`. Public subnet A uses `10.0.1.0/24` and private subnet A uses `10.0.11.0/24`. A proposed peered VPC also uses `10.0.0.0/16`, creating overlapping CIDRs that prevent straightforward routing between them.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Peering/TGW/VPN routing problems often begin with overlapping CIDRs or insufficient subnet addresses.

reveal.text: Peering/TGW/VPN routing problems often begin with overlapping CIDRs or insufficient subnet addresses.

prompts.label: WHAT IS ROUTE TABLES?
prompts.placeholder: A route table maps destination CIDR/prefixes to network targets. Routing uses the most specific matching…

reveal.text: A route table maps destination CIDR/prefixes to network targets. Routing uses the most specific matching destination route.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use route tables to determine where traffic leaves a subnet or transit attachment. Security controls…

reveal.text: Use route tables to determine where traffic leaves a subnet or transit attachment. Security controls do not replace a required route.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private subnet route table contains `10.0.0.0/16 -> local` and `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-123`.

reveal.text: A private subnet route table contains `10.0.0.0/16 -> local` and `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-123`. Traffic to another address in the VPC uses the more specific local route; internet-bound IPv4 traffic follows the NAT route.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Correct security rules but no route to the destination -> route table/path issue.

reveal.text: Correct security rules but no route to the destination -> route table/path issue.

prompts.label: ROUTE DECISION PARTS
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Destination • Target • Local route

cells.clue: IGW, NAT, TGW, endpoint, peering, etc.

cells.meaning: VPC-internal routing for the VPC CIDR.
cells.clue: Exists automatically for VPC address ranges.

prompts.label: WHAT IS SECURITY GROUPS VS NETWORK ACLS?
prompts.placeholder: Security groups are stateful allow-only controls applied to network interfaces/resources. Network ACLs are stateless subnet…

reveal.text: Security groups are stateful allow-only controls applied to network interfaces/resources. Network ACLs are stateless subnet controls with ordered allow and deny rules.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use security groups for resource-level access and NACLs for subnet-level stateless filtering or explicit deny…

reveal.text: Use security groups for resource-level access and NACLs for subnet-level stateless filtering or explicit deny patterns.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A security group allows inbound TCP/443 from clients, and response traffic is automatically allowed because the security group is stateful.

reveal.text: A security group allows inbound TCP/443 from clients, and response traffic is automatically allowed because the security group is stateful. A NACL is stateless, so its rules must also permit the required return traffic.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Security group • Network ACL

cells.use: Allow and deny rules Subnet level; numbered first-match rules

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Return traffic must be explicitly permitted by a NACL, but stateful security groups automatically allow…

reveal.text: Return traffic must be explicitly permitted by a NACL, but stateful security groups automatically allow response traffic.

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Security group • Security-group ingress • Network ACL entry • NACL rule order

reveal.code:
WebSecurityGroup:
  Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
  Properties:
    SecurityGroupIngress:
      - IpProtocol: tcp
        FromPort: 443
        ToPort: 443
        CidrIp: 203.0.113.0/24

PublicNaclEntry:
  Type: AWS::EC2::NetworkAclEntry
  Properties:
    RuleNumber: 100
    Protocol: 6
    RuleAction: allow
    Egress: false

annotations.title: Security-group ingress
annotations.explanation: Security groups use allow rules and automatically allow response traffic for established flows.

annotations.title: Network ACL entry
annotations.explanation: A NACL is a stateless subnet-level control.

annotations.title: NACL rule order
annotations.explanation: NACL entries are evaluated by rule number, with the first matching rule applied.

nodes.title: Internet gateway, NAT gateway, and egress-only IGW

prompts.label: WHAT IS INTERNET GATEWAY, NAT GATEWAY, AND EGRESS-ONLY IGW?
prompts.placeholder: An internet gateway provides a VPC path to the internet for appropriately addressed/routed resources. A…

reveal.text: An internet gateway provides a VPC path to the internet for appropriately addressed/routed resources. A NAT gateway provides initiated outbound IPv4 connectivity for private resources. An egress-only internet gateway provides outbound-only IPv6 internet connectivity.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose by IP version and whether inbound-initiated internet connectivity is required.

reveal.text: Choose by IP version and whether inbound-initiated internet connectivity is required.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private IPv4 EC2 instance downloads OS patches through a NAT gateway.

reveal.text: A private IPv4 EC2 instance downloads OS patches through a NAT gateway. A public web server with a public IPv4 address can use a route to an internet gateway. A private IPv6 workload that needs outbound-only internet uses an egress-only internet gateway.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Internet gateway • NAT gateway • Egress-only IGW

cells.use: Public IPv4/IPv6 resources when routing/addressing/security permit

cells.what: Outbound IPv4 translation for private subnets
cells.use: Private IPv4 resources need internet/AWS public endpoints

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Private subnet IPv4 patch downloads -> NAT gateway; outbound-only IPv6 -> egress-only IGW.

reveal.text: Private subnet IPv4 patch downloads -> NAT gateway; outbound-only IPv6 -> egress-only IGW.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AMAZON VPC IPAM?
prompts.placeholder: Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) helps plan, track, and monitor IP address usage across…

reveal.text: Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) helps plan, track, and monitor IP address usage across VPCs and accounts.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when a growing environment needs centralized address allocation, overlap prevention, and visibility into…

reveal.text: Use it when a growing environment needs centralized address allocation, overlap prevention, and visibility into IP utilization.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A company has 150 VPCs and keeps accidentally allocating overlapping `10.x` ranges.

reveal.text: A company has 150 VPCs and keeps accidentally allocating overlapping `10.x` ranges. VPC IPAM can centrally allocate pools, track usage, and help detect/address overlap instead of managing spreadsheets manually.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Centralized multi-account IP address planning and overlap control -> VPC IPAM.

reveal.text: Centralized multi-account IP address planning and overlap control -> VPC IPAM.

prompts.label: WHAT IS VPC ENDPOINTS AND AWS PRIVATELINK?
prompts.placeholder: A VPC endpoint lets supported traffic reach AWS or endpoint services privately without using an…

reveal.text: A VPC endpoint lets supported traffic reach AWS or endpoint services privately without using an internet gateway or NAT path. Gateway endpoints and interface endpoints work differently.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use gateway endpoints for supported S3/DynamoDB route-table integration; use interface endpoints, powered by PrivateLink, when…

reveal.text: Use gateway endpoints for supported S3/DynamoDB route-table integration; use interface endpoints, powered by PrivateLink, when the supported service is reached through private ENIs in your subnets.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Private EC2 instances download large amounts from S3.

reveal.text: Private EC2 instances download large amounts from S3. An S3 gateway endpoint lets supported S3 traffic stay on the AWS network without NAT processing. An interface endpoint instead creates private ENIs for supported PrivateLink services.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Gateway endpoint • Interface endpoint

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Reduce NAT processing for private S3 traffic -> S3 gateway endpoint.

reveal.text: Reduce NAT processing for private S3 traffic -> S3 gateway endpoint.

prompts.label: READ THE REAL CONFIG
prompts.placeholder: Key lines: Gateway endpoint • Route table association • Interface endpoint • Endpoint security group

reveal.code:
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "s3" {
  vpc_id       = aws_vpc.main.id
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Gateway"
  route_table_ids   = [aws_route_table.private.id]
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "service" {
  vpc_id              = aws_vpc.main.id
  service_name        = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0123456789abcdef0"
  vpc_endpoint_type   = "Interface"
  subnet_ids          = [aws_subnet.private_a.id]
  security_group_ids  = [aws_security_group.endpoint.id]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}

prompts.label: WHAT IS VPC PEERING VS TRANSIT GATEWAY?
prompts.placeholder: VPC peering is a direct point-to-point VPC connection and is not transitive. Transit Gateway is…

reveal.text: VPC peering is a direct point-to-point VPC connection and is not transitive. Transit Gateway is a hub that connects many VPCs and hybrid networks with centralized routing.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use peering for a limited number of direct connections; use Transit Gateway when many networks…

reveal.text: Use peering for a limited number of direct connections; use Transit Gateway when many networks need hub-and-spoke connectivity and centralized routing.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: VPC A peers with B and B peers with C.

reveal.text: VPC A peers with B and B peers with C. A cannot use B as a transit router to reach C because peering is non-transitive. A Transit Gateway can provide hub-and-spoke transit routing for many VPCs.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: VPC peering • Transit Gateway

cells.use: Many VPC/hybrid attachments with transit routing

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Dozens of VPCs with full mesh requirements -> Transit Gateway usually reduces connection complexity.

reveal.text: Dozens of VPCs with full mesh requirements -> Transit Gateway usually reduces connection complexity.

nodes.title: WAF, Shield, Network Firewall, and DNS Firewall

prompts.label: WHAT IS WAF, SHIELD, NETWORK FIREWALL, AND DNS FIREWALL?
prompts.placeholder: AWS network-protection services operate at different layers: WAF filters HTTP(S), Shield provides DDoS protections, Network…

reveal.text: AWS network-protection services work at different layers. AWS WAF filters HTTP(S) requests. AWS Shield helps protect against DDoS attacks. AWS Network Firewall filters VPC traffic. Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall controls DNS queries to domains.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose the service from the traffic/protection layer being controlled.

reveal.text: Choose the service from the traffic/protection layer being controlled.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: WAF filters web requests; Shield addresses DDoS; Network Firewall filters VPC traffic; DNS Firewall blocks domains.

reveal.text: AWS WAF blocks a malicious HTTP request pattern. AWS Shield helps protect against DDoS attacks. Network Firewall inspects VPC traffic. Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall blocks queries to a known malicious domain.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: AWS WAF • AWS Shield • AWS Network Firewall • DNS Firewall

cells.what: DNS domain queries through Route 53 Resolver

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Block DNS requests to known malicious domains -> Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall.

reveal.text: Block DNS requests to known malicious domains -> Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall.

prompts.label: WHAT IS NETWORK COST OPTIMIZATION?
prompts.placeholder: Network architecture affects cost through data-transfer paths and processing services such as NAT gateways.

reveal.text: Network architecture affects cost through data-transfer paths and processing services such as NAT gateways.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Look for unnecessary cross-AZ traffic, large NAT-processed transfers to supported AWS services, avoidable public paths…

reveal.text: Look for unnecessary cross-AZ traffic, large NAT-processed transfers to supported AWS services, avoidable public paths, and topology that sends traffic through extra processing hops.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Private instances send 8 TB/day to S3 through a NAT gateway.

reveal.text: Private instances send 8 TB/day to S3 through a NAT gateway. Using an S3 gateway endpoint can remove unnecessary NAT processing from that path and reduce cost while keeping supported traffic private.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Private EC2 transfers terabytes to S3 through NAT -> consider an S3 gateway endpoint.

reveal.text: Private EC2 transfers terabytes to S3 through NAT -> consider an S3 gateway endpoint.

prompts.label: WHAT IS ROUTE 53 HOSTED ZONES AND RECORDS?
prompts.placeholder: A Route 53 hosted zone stores DNS records for a domain. Public hosted zones answer…

reveal.text: A Route 53 hosted zone stores DNS records for a domain. Public hosted zones answer on the public internet; private hosted zones answer inside associated VPC environments.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use alias records for supported AWS targets when appropriate, including zone-apex cases where a CNAME…

reveal.text: Use alias records for supported AWS targets when appropriate, including zone-apex cases where a CNAME cannot be used.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A private hosted zone contains `db.internal.example.com -> 10.0.20.15` and resolves only inside associated VPCs.

reveal.text: A private hosted zone contains `db.internal.example.com -> 10.0.20.15` and resolves only inside associated VPCs. A public hosted zone for `www.example.com` answers users on the public internet.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Public hosted zone • Private hosted zone

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Internal-only DNS name for VPC workloads -> private hosted zone.

reveal.text: Internal-only DNS name for VPC workloads -> private hosted zone.

prompts.label: WHAT IS ROUTE 53 RESOLVER ENDPOINTS?
prompts.placeholder: Route 53 Resolver handles DNS resolution for VPCs. Inbound endpoints let on-premises networks query VPC/Route…

reveal.text: Route 53 Resolver handles DNS resolution for VPCs. Inbound endpoints let on-premises networks query VPC/Route 53 Resolver names; outbound endpoints forward selected VPC queries to external DNS resolvers.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Resolver rules with outbound endpoints for hybrid DNS forwarding and inbound endpoints for on-premises-to-AWS…

reveal.text: Use Resolver rules with outbound endpoints for hybrid DNS forwarding and inbound endpoints for on-premises-to-AWS private DNS resolution.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: An EC2 instance queries `db.corp.example`.

reveal.text: An EC2 instance queries `db.corp.example`. A Resolver forwarding rule matches `corp.example` and sends the query through an outbound Resolver endpoint to on-premises DNS at `10.20.0.53`.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Inbound endpoint • Outbound endpoint

cells.use: Resolve AWS/VPC private names from external networks
Forward selected domains out of AWS

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: VPC workloads need to resolve corp.example on-prem -> outbound Resolver endpoint + forwarding rule.

reveal.text: VPC workloads need to resolve corp.example on-prem -> outbound Resolver endpoint + forwarding rule.

prompts.label: HYBRID DNS DIRECTION
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Inbound Resolver endpoint • Outbound Resolver endpoint

cells.fit: External networks must resolve private AWS/VPC names.
VPC workloads must resolve corporate/on-prem domains.

items: Query goes through inbound/outbound path as designed

nodes.title: Route 53 routing policies and query logging

prompts.label: WHAT IS ROUTE 53 ROUTING POLICIES AND QUERY LOGGING?
prompts.placeholder: Route 53 routing policies decide how DNS answers are selected. Query logging records DNS-query information…

reveal.text: Route 53 routing policies decide how DNS answers are selected. Query logging records DNS-query information for investigation.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, or multivalue behavior based on the routing requirement…

reveal.text: Choose simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, or multivalue behavior based on the routing requirement and health needs.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A weighted policy sends 90% of DNS responses to the current version and 10% to a new endpoint.

reveal.text: A weighted policy sends 90% of DNS responses to the current version and 10% to a new endpoint. A failover policy instead uses primary/secondary health, while latency routing chooses a Region based on measured DNS routing latency.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Percentage traffic split -> weighted; active/passive -> failover; lowest network latency -> latency routing.

reveal.text: Percentage traffic split -> weighted; active/passive -> failover; lowest network latency -> latency routing.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AMAZON CLOUDFRONT?
prompts.placeholder: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) that serves content through edge locations and…

reveal.text: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network (CDN) that serves content through edge locations and can cache responses close to viewers.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for HTTP(S) content distribution, caching, lower origin load, and edge-integrated controls.

reveal.text: Use it for HTTP(S) content distribution, caching, lower origin load, and edge-integrated controls.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A user in Tokyo requests `/app.js`.

reveal.text: A user in Tokyo requests `/app.js`. CloudFront serves a cached copy from a nearby edge location instead of fetching from the origin on every request, reducing latency and origin load.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Cache static/dynamic HTTP content near users -> CloudFront.

reveal.text: Cache static/dynamic HTTP content near users -> CloudFront.

prompts.label: WHAT IS AWS GLOBAL ACCELERATOR?
prompts.placeholder: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global…

reveal.text: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global network to healthy regional endpoints. It is not an object cache.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use it when applications need improved global network-path performance or stable global IP entry points…

reveal.text: Use it when applications need improved global network-path performance or stable global IP entry points without CDN object caching.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A global TCP game service needs two static anycast IP addresses and faster paths to healthy endpoints in `us-east-1` and `eu-west-1`.

reveal.text: A global TCP game service needs two static anycast IP addresses and faster paths to healthy endpoints in `us-east-1` and `eu-west-1`. Global Accelerator fits because the requirement is network-path acceleration, not object caching.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: CloudFront • Global Accelerator

cells.what: Network-path acceleration and static anycast IPs
cells.use: Route to healthy regional endpoints; no object cache

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Need static global anycast IPs and accelerated TCP/UDP or non-cache use -> Global Accelerator.

reveal.text: Need static global anycast IPs and accelerated TCP/UDP or non-cache use -> Global Accelerator.

prompts.label: STATIC IP CHOICES
prompts.placeholder: Elastic IP = one static public IPv4 address for a regional resource • Global Accelerator = global anycast IP entry points across healthy endpoints.

cells.use: One regional resource needs a stable public IPv4 address
Global clients need stable entry IPs and AWS-network routing to healthy regional endpoints

prompts.label: WHAT IS VPC PATH TROUBLESHOOTING?
prompts.placeholder: Network troubleshooting should trace the path layer by layer: DNS, routing, security groups, NACLs, endpoint/load-balancer…

reveal.text: Network troubleshooting should trace the path layer by layer: DNS, routing, security groups, NACLs, endpoint/load-balancer health, and return path.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use evidence to find the first failing layer rather than changing multiple controls at once.

reveal.text: Use evidence to find the first failing layer rather than changing multiple controls at once.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A client cannot reach an ALB.

reveal.text: A client cannot reach an ALB. DNS resolves correctly, but the subnet route is valid and the security group denies the client port. Walking DNS -> route -> SG/NACL -> target health finds the first failing layer instead of randomly changing settings.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Resolve -> route -> filter -> target health -> return path is a reliable troubleshooting…

reveal.text: Resolve -> route -> filter -> target health -> return path is a reliable troubleshooting order.

prompts.label: HOW IT FLOWS
prompts.placeholder: Flow: Resolve DNS → … → Check return path

prompts.label: WHAT IS VPC FLOW LOGS?
prompts.placeholder: VPC Flow Logs record network-flow metadata such as source/destination addresses, ports, protocol, bytes/packets, and accept/reject…

reveal.text: VPC Flow Logs record network-flow metadata such as source/destination addresses, ports, protocol, bytes/packets, and accept/reject decisions for supported network interfaces/resources. They do not capture application payloads.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use them to see whether traffic reached an interface and whether network filtering accepted or…

reveal.text: Use them to see whether traffic reached an interface and whether network filtering accepted or rejected the flow.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A VPC Flow Log record shows source `10.0.1.10`, destination `10.0.2.20`, destination port `443`, and action `REJECT`.

reveal.text: A VPC Flow Log record shows source `10.0.1.10`, destination `10.0.2.20`, destination port `443`, and action `REJECT`. That proves network filtering rejected the flow, but it does not show the HTTP request body.

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Need accept/reject metadata for network flows -> VPC Flow Logs.

reveal.text: Need accept/reject metadata for network flows -> VPC Flow Logs.

prompts.label: WHAT IS REACHABILITY ANALYZER AND SERVICE LOGS?
prompts.placeholder: VPC Reachability Analyzer evaluates configured network paths to explain whether a source can reach a…

reveal.text: VPC Reachability Analyzer evaluates configured network paths to explain whether a source can reach a destination. Service logs show observed requests and rule decisions.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Use Reachability Analyzer for configuration/path reasoning; use ELB/WAF/CloudFront/application logs when you need evidence of requests…

reveal.text: Use Reachability Analyzer for configuration/path reasoning; use ELB/WAF/CloudFront/application logs when you need evidence of requests that actually occurred.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: Reachability Analyzer reports that a source ENI cannot reach a destination because the route table has no matching route.

reveal.text: Reachability Analyzer reports that a source ENI cannot reach a destination because the route table has no matching route. It reasons from configuration without needing to generate test packets. Flow Logs answer a different question: what traffic was actually observed.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Reachability Analyzer • Flow/service logs

cells.use: Would the network configuration allow this path?

nodes.title: Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN, and Client VPN

prompts.label: WHAT IS DIRECT CONNECT, SITE-TO-SITE VPN, AND CLIENT VPN?
prompts.placeholder: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity between customer networks and AWS. Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec network-to-network…

reveal.text: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity between customer networks and AWS. Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec network-to-network connectivity over the internet. Client VPN provides secure remote-user/device access.

prompts.label: WHEN DOES IT MATTER?
prompts.placeholder: Choose based on who is connecting and whether dedicated private connectivity or internet-based encrypted connectivity…

reveal.text: Choose based on who is connecting and whether dedicated private connectivity or internet-based encrypted connectivity is required.

prompts.label: CONCRETE EXAMPLE
prompts.placeholder: A data center needs stable dedicated connectivity for large daily transfers: Direct Connect may fit.

reveal.text: A data center needs stable dedicated connectivity for large daily transfers: Direct Connect may fit. A branch office needs encrypted network-to-network connectivity over the internet: Site-to-Site VPN. Remote employees need user VPN access: Client VPN.

prompts.label: DON'T CONFUSE THESE
prompts.placeholder: Compare: Direct Connect • Site-to-Site VPN • Client VPN

prompts.label: EXAM / SCENARIO CLUE
prompts.placeholder: Remote employees need VPN access -> Client VPN; data-center network to VPC -> Site-to-Site VPN…
